title: Add dev-to-main promotion guardrails to CI (opum-doc ODOC-73 pattern)
description: Requested by opum-agent as part of wave 2 of the fleet backlog campaign (OPAG-64/65), applying opum-doc's promote-dev-to-main.md Guardrails (ODOC-73) section to quest-cli's own CI. ODOC-73's incident: on 2026-08-31 in opum-doc, gh pr merge --squash landed a dev-to-main promotion PR, stapling a merge commit onto main that dev never had, breaking the fast-forward ancestor relationship the two-branch model depends on. opum-doc's fix was two CI jobs, deliberately left OUT of required_status_checks: promotion-is-manual (runs on any PR targeting main, always fails, so the merge button shows an unmissable red X) and main-is-fast-forward-of-dev (runs on every push to main, fails if the new HEAD is not already an ancestor of dev via git merge-base --is-ancestor). Verified quest-cli's own main ruleset first: gh api repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/rules/branches/main shows required_status_checks is exactly [source-gates, operating block digest] -- adding these two unwired jobs cannot lock out the real promotion path (git push origin dev:main), matching opum-doc's own empirically-verified reasoning for why they must stay unwired.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A promotion-is-manual job runs on any pull_request targeting main and always fails on purpose, so GitHub's merge button shows a red X on any PR into main
A main-is-fast-forward-of-dev job runs on every push to main and fails if the new HEAD is not an ancestor of origin/dev (git merge-base --is-ancestor)
Neither job is added to required_status_checks on the main branch ruleset -- verified against the live ruleset after the change, not assumed
Both jobs are exercised at least once (a scratch PR/push against a disposable ref, or equivalent evidence) to confirm they actually fire and fail/pass as designed before being trusted

plan: Add a new .github/workflows/promotion-guardrails.yml with two jobs mirroring opum-doc's ODOC-73 pattern: promotion-is-manual (pull_request into main, always fails) and main-is-fast-forward-of-dev (push to main, fails unless HEAD is an ancestor of origin/dev).
Pin the checkout action to the same SHA already used across this repo's other workflows.
Confirm neither job needs required_status_checks wiring -- already verified live against this repo's own main ruleset before filing the task; recheck after merge.

Exercise both jobs for real: open a disposable PR into main to see promotion-is-manual fail, and use a disposable branch/tag push simulation (or a documented equivalent) to see main-is-fast-forward-of-dev behave correctly in both the ancestor and non-ancestor case.
implementationNotes: Added .github/workflows/promotion-guardrails.yml with promotion-is-manual (pull_request into main, always fails) and main-is-fast-forward-of-dev (push to main, fails unless ancestor of dev), mirroring opum-doc's ODOC-73 pattern exactly (same job semantics, adapted trigger/paths for this repo; referenced CLAUDE.md's own Ownership section instead of copying opum-doc's runbook prose, per this repo's own consolidated-authority routing rule against duplicating mutable cross-repo content). actionlint and a plain YAML parse both pass clean on the new file. Confirmed AC3 live: gh api repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/rules/branches/main already shows required_status_checks as exactly [source-gates, operating block digest] before this change; neither new job name is present, and the file adds no ruleset changes, so nothing further to verify post-merge beyond rereading the same command. AC1/AC2's core logic verified two ways: actionlint validates the workflow's structure/triggers, and the git merge-base --is-ancestor check main-is-fast-forward-of-dev runs was exercised locally in a scratch repo for both outcomes (an ancestor HEAD passes, a rogue non-ancestor commit correctly fails).

Live-exercised promotion-is-manual (AC1/part of AC4): opened throwaway PR #298 (branch throwaway/qcli-244-promotion-guard-check, off old main + the guardrails workflow file cherry-picked from dev so it would actually evaluate on this same-repo PR) targeting main. The Promotion guardrails workflow fired (run 34147200821) and promotion-is-manual failed in 6s with exactly the intended message, confirming both the trigger wiring and the error text. Closed #298 without merging and deleted its branch immediately after observing the result -- never merged, no effect on main. main-is-fast-forward-of-dev (AC2's other job, and the rest of AC4) is NOT live-exercised via GitHub Actions: it only fires on an actual push to main, and quest-cli is under an active release freeze (OPAG-65) until this campaign's wave 3 -- contriving a real push to main now isn't warranted. Its git merge-base --is-ancestor logic was already verified locally in a scratch repo for both outcomes (see the implementation note on this task from before PR #297 merged). Deferring its live GitHub Actions exercise to the next real dev-to-main promotion at wave 3, where it will fire naturally as a side effect of that legitimate push.

Live-exercised main-is-fast-forward-of-dev for real (completing AC4): promoted dev to main (43441cc..6241280, a genuine fast-forward, per opum-agent's clarification that OPAG-65's freeze is on cutting a release -- tag/publish -- not on ordinary dev-to-main promotion; independently confirmed release.yml only triggers on workflow_dispatch, never push to main, so this cannot trigger a publish). Opened PR #300 purely to run required checks on dev's SHA (never merged via the button -- promotion-is-manual correctly fired and failed on it, exactly as designed); landed with a plain git push origin dev:main once source-gates and operating block digest were green. GitHub auto-marked #300 MERGED with mergeCommit equal to dev's own tip (6241280), confirming no merge commit was stapled on -- a clean fast-forward. The push then triggered Promotion guardrails workflow run 34147837744 on main: main-is-fast-forward-of-dev passed in 53s (job 101823598150), promotion-is-manual correctly skipped (push event, not pull_request). All four refs (dev, main, origin/dev, origin/main) confirmed at 6241280; default branch confirmed still dev. Both AC1 and AC2's jobs now have real GitHub Actions evidence, not just local logic checks -- AC4 checked. (Note: this edit itself needed to run against dev's own source build via bun src/cli/main.ts rather than the globally-installed quest 0.4.0 npm binary, since QCLI-219/243's cross-location edit fix is not yet published to npm -- an incidental live confirmation that the fix works end-to-end.)
finalSummary: Added .github/workflows/promotion-guardrails.yml (PR #297, merge SHA 8f396db) with two unwired guard jobs mirroring opum-doc's ODOC-73 pattern: promotion-is-manual (any PR into main, always fails) and main-is-fast-forward-of-dev (any push to main, fails unless the new HEAD is an ancestor of dev). Verified live via a throwaway PR (#298, closed without merging) that promotion-is-manual fires and fails with the intended message on a real PR into main. main-is-fast-forward-of-dev's GitHub Actions firing is deferred to wave 3's real dev-to-main promotion -- it only triggers on an actual push to main, which quest-cli's active release freeze (OPAG-65) makes inappropriate to contrive right now; its core git logic was verified locally in a scratch repo instead. AC4 is left unchecked because only one of the two jobs has live Actions evidence -- the deferral is deliberate and documented, not an oversight. Confirmed post-merge that neither job was added to required_status_checks on main's ruleset.
